items.title: T.V.M
items.decryption: T: Thinnai (Porches for gatherings), V: Viragal (Hero Stones), M: Mandapam (Open-pillared halls).

items: Do not confuse Sangam-era rock-cut art with the later Pallava monolithic rathas.
Sangam architecture was primarily perishable (wood/brick/mud); stone temples are mostly post-Sangam.
Avoid assuming Dravidian 'Gopurams' existed in the Sangam age; these are medieval evolutions.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Centered in Tamilagam (TN, Kerala, parts of AP/Karnataka)
  • 5 Thinai landscapes shaped aesthetic motifs

Artistic Focus

  • Hero Stones (Viragal)
  • Wooden Palaces
  • Floral and Avian motifs

Architectural Evolution Mindmap

  • Materials:
    • Wood, Brick, Mud, and Ivory
    • Lack of durable stone architecture
  • Types of Structures:
    • Viragal: Commemorating warriors (Hero Stones).
    • Mandapams: Pillared community halls.
    • Royal Palaces: Elaborate multi-storeyed wooden buildings mentioned in Silappadikaram.
FeatureSangam Period Status
Temple Towers (Vimana)Absent (Pre-Temple era)
SculptureHero Stones (Viragal) focus
Primary MaterialWood and Mud
